patterns.comment: A network-text network — the textual form of an FBD/LD body, network text v2 (volt-cli docs/network-text-next.html). Detected by content (the NETWORK header at a line start), so it lights up in any graphical body. The header carries no order number and no language (the body's `(* @volt-implementation FBD|LD *)` marker says it once); its optional fields are NAMED and come in one order — LABEL: is the jump target, TITLE: is free text with ST's $-escapes, DISABLED the vendor's bit — and it ends at its newline. `\b` after NETWORK keeps a variable such as NETWORK_OK an identifier. Mirrors the LSP's network-text parser header.
patterns.name: meta.network.vg

patterns.comment: The network's wire block: `VAR_TEMP g1, g2 : BOOL; END_VAR`, one per network that has a Demux. Its names are the network's WIRES (g<digits>, the vendor VarId), coloured apart from the type the rest of the ST grammar colours. A reference to a wire elsewhere is told from a variable by the LSP's `wire` semantic token, which resolves it through the network's scope — a name pattern alone would also paint a POU variable called g2.
patterns.name: meta.wires.vg

patterns.comment: Backticked text is ONE operand, target or call head whose text is not a single token (`fc_dinttotime(T.Start,2)`, `arr[i + 1]`) — verbatim between the backticks, never parsed into boxes. Matched before the ST grammar so its parentheses and operators are not coloured as structure.
patterns.name: variable.other.quoted.vg

patterns.comment: `.ENO` — a consumer connected to the box's ENO output. An output of the box, not a member of its result.
patterns.name: keyword.other.eno.vg

patterns.comment: The text's own constructs, call-shaped: R_EDGE(x) / F_EDGE(x) are edge FLAGS on their operand (not an R_TRIG box), PARALLEL(…) is the LD BoxTreeParallel. Only followed by `(`, and never as part of a longer name.
patterns.name: keyword.other.construct.vg
